ABS.title: Total Absorption
ABS.description: Total absorption is retrieved from the absorption of light by particulate and dissolved organic and inorganic matter at a specific reference wavelength, defined at 440nm.

AOT.title: Aerosol Optical Thickness
AOT.description: Aerosol Optical Thickness is the degree to which aerosols in the atmosphere prevent the transmission of light by absorption or scattering.

BAT-TOP.title: Bathymetry from nautical charts and single-beam transects

BBA.title: Backscattering / Absorption Ratio
BBA.description: Ratio of total backscattering and total absorption

CDM.title: CDOM, Yellow substance
CDM.description: CDM comprises all colored dissolved organic matter (CDOM) which influences the water color. It is measured in terms of absorption at a specific reference wavelength, defined at 440nm.

CHA.title: Chlorophyll-a
CHA.description: Chlorophyll-a is based on the derived information of the pigment-specific in-water absorption, in-water turbidity and spectral characteristics of each water body.

CHC.title: Cyano-Chlorophyll
CHC.description: Cyano-Chlorophyll is based on the derived information of the pigment-specific in-water absorption of Phycoerythrin, a pigment commonly found in cyanobacteria, in-water turbidity and spectral characteristics of each water body.

CHL.title: Total Chlorophyll
CHL.description: Total Chlorophyll is based on the derived information of in-water organic absorption, in-water turbidity and spectral characteristics of each water body.

DIV.title: Organic Absorption / Turbidity
DIV.description: DIV is the ratio between total absorption and total scattering of water constituents at 550nm. Zones of increased DIV can therefore be interpreted as zones of increased organic production or increased dissolved organic and nutrient inflows, independent on absolute concentrations.

DSM-MSB.title: Merged digital surface model and multi-source bathymetry

DSM-SDB.title: Merged digital surface model and satellite-derived bathymetry

EVA.title: Evaporation Rate
EVA.description: Evaporation Rate is calculated using Sea Surface Temperature (SST) and additional weather data, downloadable as a 3-hourly global dataset with a grid size of 0.25 degree (http://hydro1.gesdisc.eosdis.nasa.gov/data/GLDAS/GLDAS_NOAH025_3H.2.1).

EVI.title: Enhanced Vegetation Index
EVI.description:
The EVI is a vegetation index with improved sensitivity in high biomass regions. It was once developed mainly for use with MODIS and is calculated from atmospherically corrected surface reflectances following the formula: EVI = G * ((NIR -RED) / (NIR + C1 * RED -C2 * BLUE +L)) with the coefficients set to: 
G = 2.5 
C1 = 6 
C2 = 7.5 
L = 1

FAI.title: Floating Algae Index
FAI.description: The FAI is an index sensitive to floating algae, such as Sargassum, using the red, red-edge, near-infrared and short-wave infrared bands (depending on available channels of the respective sensor).

GND.title: Green Normalized Difference Vegetation Index
GND.description: NDVI is a very basic vegetation index, calculated from atmospherically corrected surface reflectances. The GNDVI follows the exact same principle, but uses the green band instead of the red band, following the formula: GNDVI = (NIR - GREEN) / (NIR + GREEN).

GSA.title: Green Soil-adjusted Vegetation Index
GSA.description:
The SAVI is a basic vegetation index that takes the influence of different soil colors into account, compared to, e.g., NDVI. It was originally established by Huete (1988) and is calculated from atmospherically corrected surface reflectances. The GSAVI follows the exact same principle, but uses the green band instead of the red band, following the formula: GSAVI = (NIR - GREEN) / (NIR + GREEN + L) * (1 + L) 
L is the canopy background adjustment factor and is commonly used with a value of 0.5.

HAB.title: Harmful Algae Bloom Indicator
HAB.description:
The algorithm detects areas likely affected by harmful algae blooms formed by cyanobacteria containing phycocyanin pigments by analyzing spectral trends in the green-red wavelength bands as a proxy. The classification reads as follows: 
1: no HAB (probability 0) 
2: HAB unlikely (probability 0.2) 
3: HAB likely (probability 0.5) 
4: HAB very likely (probabilty greater 0.5).

KDB.title: Diffuse Attenuation Coefficient (490nm)
KDB.description: KDB is the diffuse attenuation coefficient for the 'blue' channel (around 490nm) and is also referred to as Kd490. The exact wavelength can differ slightly between sensors, depending on their respective spectral properties.

KDC.title: Diffuse Attenuation Coefficient
KDC.description: KDC is the diffuse attenuation coefficient and is given for each sensor channel of the visible spectrum. The distinct wavelengths of these channels slightly differ between the sensors.

KDP.title: Diffuse Attenuation Coefficient (of photosynthetically available radiation)
KDP.description: KDP is the diffuse attenuation coefficient of the photosynthetically available radiation (usually between 490 and 670nm).

LRF.title: Land Reflectance
LRF.description: Surface reflectance (after atmospheric correction) over non-water surfaces (typically land).

LULC.title: Land use and land cover classification

LWR.title: Land Water Reflectance
LWR.description: Surface reflectance after atmospheric correction. LWR is a combination of the land and water reflectance products (LRF and RRA).

MLO.title: Machine Learning Output
MLO.description: Output from EOMAP's Machine Learning Algorithm. The actual content and its units depend on the input data.

NDV.title: Normalized Difference Vegetation Index
NDV.description: NDVI is a very basic vegetation index, calculated from atmospherically corrected surface reflectances following the formula: NDVI = (NIR - RED) / (NIR + RED).

NDW.title: Normalized Difference Water Index
NDW.description: NDWI as calculated by EOMAP refers to water content in leaves and is calculated from atmospherically corrected surface reflectances following the formula: NDWI = (NIR - SWIR) / (NIR + SWIR).

NRF.title: Normed Remote Sensing Reflectance
NRF.description: Remote sensing reflectance (pi * RRS[0, 0]), normed to a sun angle of 0 degrees (nadir).

NRG.title: False Color Quicklook image
NRG.description: Composite image, representing the satellite image either in false color mode depending on the used sensor. In most cases, the spectral band from the near-infrared and visible spectrum are used (red and green).

OTC.title: OLCI Terrestrial Chlorophyll Index
OTC.description:
OTCI is a chlorophyll index specifically designed for Sentinel-3. It is calculated from atmospherically corrected surface reflectance following the formula: OTCI = (NIR -REDEDGE) / (REDEDGE - RED); in case of Sentinel-3, the bands are: 
RED = Band 10 (681nm) 
REDEDGE = Band 11 (709nm) 
NIR = Band 12 (753nm).

OWD.title: Optical Water Depth
OWD.description: Optical water depth or bathymetry, corrected for lowest astronomical tide (LAT). Negative values: water depth. Positive values: intertidal zone (elevation above LAT).

QUA.title: Quality Assessment
QUA.description: Quality assessment per pixel, based on illumination, geometry, atmospheric properties, spatial noise, among others. The first channel always holds the combined total quality, while all other channels hold more detailed information for each specific quality check.

QUC.title: EOMAP Quality Coding
QUC.description: EOMAP Quality Coding gives information about quality risks and specific quality flags for each pixel.

QUT.title: Total Quality
QUT.description: Quality estimation expressed in greyvalues in 8 bit, ranging from 1 (lowest quality) to 100 (highest quality). 0 represents land, clouds or flagged pixels.

RGB.title: RGB composite image
RGB.description: The Composite image represents the satellite image either in true or false color mode depending on the used sensor. In most cases, the spectral bands from the visible spectrum are used (red, green, and blue).

RRA.title: Remote Sensing Reflectance (above-surface, Nadir)
RRA.description: Above-surface remote sensing reflectance [RRA (0+)], defined as Lu/Ed, with nadir view angle.

RRS.title: Remote Sensing Reflectance (sub-surface)
RRS.description: Sub-surface remote sensing reflectance [RRS (0-)], defined as Lu/Ed, with nadir view angle.

RRW.title: Remote Sensing Reflectance (above-surface, WISP)
RRW.description: Above-surface remote sensing reflectance [RRW (0+)], defined as Lu/Ed, with view angle according to WISP configuration.

SAV.title: Soil-adjusted Vegetation Index
SAV.description: The SAVI is a basic vegetation index that takes the influence of different soil colors into account, compared to, e.g., NDVI. It was originally established by Huete (1988) and is calculated from atmospherically corrected surface reflectances, following the formula: SAVI = (1 + L) * (NIR - RED) / (NIR + RED + L). L is the canopy background adjustment factor and is commonly used with a value of 0.5.

SCI.title: Scientific RRSAB
SCI.description: Scientific image that contains different RRSAB spectra as well as atmospheric and in-water parameters.

SDB.title: Satellite-derived bathymetry
SDB.description: Water depth derived from optical satellite image data with EOMAP's Modular Inversion System (MIP), a physics-based method that separates the light reflected by the sea floor from atmosphere, water surface and water column. Negative values are depths below the vertical datum of the asset.

SDD.title: Secchi Disk Depth
SDD.description: Secchi Disk Depth or transparency indicates the clarity of the water column. The related measure of Secchi Depth (measured with a Secchi Disk) is a common parameter in water quality analysis.

SEM.title: Seamless Elevation Model
SEM.description: Elevation model that seamlessly connects land elevation and water depth (bathymetry).

SIA.title: Sum of Inorganic Absorbers
SIA.description: The sum of inorganic absorption is retrieved from the absorption of light by particulate and dissolved inorganic matter at a specific reference wavelength, defined at 440nm.

SLP.title: Aerosol Slope Modifier
SLP.description: Atmospheric absorption from aerosols is wavelength-dependent. The change of this dependency in terms of deviation from EOMAPs standard aerosol model is expressed as the aerosol slope modifier.

SOA.title: Sum of Organic Absorbers
SOA.description: The sum of organic absorption is retrieved from the absorption of light by particulate and dissolved organic matter at a specific reference wavelength, defined at 440nm.

SSR.title: Subsurface reflectance
SSR.description: Sub-surface irradiance reflectance [SSR (0-)], defined as Eu/Ed (unitless).

SST.title: Sea Surface Temperature
SST.description: Sea/Water Surface Temperature is calculated from thermal infrared channels. SST from Landsat is directly taken from Level-2 data, provided by USGS.

TSC.title: Trophic State Index
TSC.description:
Trophic State Index range from 0 to 100 
0-39: oligotrophic 
40-59: mesotrophic 
60-79: eutrophic 
80+: hypereutrophic

TSM.title: Total suspended matter
TSM.description: TSM is essentially related to the total scattering of particles in the water column and determined by the backward scattering of light in the visible region.

TUR.title: Turbidity
TUR.description: Turbidity is derived from the scattering caused by suspended particles in water and determined by the backward scattering of light between 450 to 800nm.

WEX.title: Water Body Extent
WEX.description:
Water Body Extent product discriminates between land/clouds and water pixels based on typical reflectance features in visible and near/shortwave infrared region. 
land/clouds = 0 
water = 1

Z90.title: Signal Depth (z90)
Z90.description: Z90 indicates the water depth from which 90% of the reflected light originates.
